title: Restricted internal scalar extension equals relative tensor, naturally
statement:
Let $C$ be an essentially small site, and let $H=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ have the canonical sheafified tensor over $\mathbf Z$, with sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal structure as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the coequalizer relative tensor and its induced monoidal structure [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For any commutative ring object $R$, write $U:\operatorname{Mod}_R(H)\to H$ for the forgetful functor and $t_{P,M}:UP\otimes UM\to U(P\otimes_R M)$ for the canonical coequalizer projection.
Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, let $N=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(B)$ be the restricted regular module, and use scalar extension and restriction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Put $E(M)=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi M)$ and let $p_M:B\otimes UM\to UE(M)$ be the scalar-extension coequalizer projection. There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$\kappa:E\xrightarrow{\sim}N\otimes_R-$$
whose components satisfy, as morphisms in $H$,
$$U(\kappa_M)\circ p_M=t_{N,M},\qquad U(\kappa_M^{-1})\circ t_{N,M}=p_M.$$
In particular both components are $R$-linear and mutually inverse. Explicitly its naturality says that for every $R$-linear map $f:M\to M'$, one has
$$\kappa_{M'}\circ E(f)=(\operatorname{id}_N\otimes_R f)\circ\kappa_M.$$
No freeness hypothesis on $B$ over $R$ is imposed, and these equations are identities of sheaf morphisms, not an identification of tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensor products.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference, identification of restricted scalar extension with tensor by the restricted regular algebra; current item proof steps 2 and comparison-naturality part of 6

proof.text:
Write $\gamma_N=\mu_B\circ(\varphi\otimes1_B)$, by restriction of the regular action. Naturality of the braiding and commutativity of $B$ give the following equality of morphisms $B\otimes R\to B$:
$$\rho_N:=\gamma_N\circ\beta_{B,R}=\mu_B\circ\beta_{B,B}\circ(1_B\otimes\varphi)=\mu_B\circ(1_B\otimes\varphi).$$
This computes the right action used in the relative tensor; no sectionwise tensor identification is involved.

source.place: Restriction clause 1; relative-tensor definition, right action on the first factor

proof.text:
For each $M$, put $D_M=(B\otimes R)\otimes UM$, $V_M=B\otimes UM$, and
$$a_M=\rho_N\otimes1_{UM},\qquad b_M=(1_B\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha_{B,R,UM}:D_M\rightrightarrows V_M.$$
The relative-tensor definition says $t_M:=t_{N,M}$ is a coequalizer of this pair. The extension definition and step 1 say that $p_M$ is a coequalizer of exactly the same pair. Restriction leaves the underlying object and projection unchanged.

source.place: Displayed coequalizer, compared with the displayed relative-tensor coequalizer

proof.text: For each M, descend the tensor projection t_M through the extension coequalizer p_M to obtain f_M, and descend p_M through t_M to obtain g_M. Step 2 identifies the balancing pairs, so both descents exist. Their normalization equations are p_M f_M = t_M and t_M g_M = p_M. Precomposing f_M g_M and g_M f_M with p_M and t_M, respectively, makes each the identity. Cancel the coequalizer projections. In Lean these are extendDescHom, coequalizer.desc, extendπ_extendDescHom, coequalizer.π_desc and cancel_epi.

source.place: Tag 002A, coequalizer universal property and uniqueness

proof.text: The forward comparison is R-linear. Precompose its action equation with R tensor p_M, which is epic because tensor preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Restriction writes the extension action as (phi tensor 1) followed by its B-action. Move phi past the tensor of p_M by bifunctoriality and use whiskerLeft_extendπ_smul. On the relative-tensor side use whiskerLeft_tensorπ_smul. Substitute p_M f_M = t_M; associator naturality identifies the remaining composites with the action gamma_N = mu_B (phi tensor 1). Cancel R tensor p_M. Apply Mod.isoMk to the underlying isomorphism to obtain an R-module isomorphism; the inverse is linear by the inverse identities.

source.place: First-factor action and restriction formula; relative-tensor first-factor action

proof.text: For an R-module morphism u:M to M\prime, precompose the naturality equation with p_M. By extendπ_extendScalarsMap the extension map sends p_M to (1_B tensor u) p_M\prime; by tensorObjπ_whiskerLeft the relative tensor map sends t_M to (1_B tensor u) t_M\prime. The factorization equation p_M f_M = t_M now identifies the composites, so cancellation of p_M proves naturality. NatIso.ofComponents assembles the module isomorphisms. The normalization equations from step 3 give both displayed assertions. No colimit over the module category and no freeness hypothesis is used.
